title: Bag of Tokens
statement:
You hold an amount of energy `power`, a score that begins at `0`, and a bag of tokens whose values are given by the integer array `tokens`. You may use the tokens one at a time, in any order, and each token can be used at most once, in exactly one of two ways:

- **Face-up:** allowed only when your power is at least `tokens[i]`; your power drops by `tokens[i]` and your score rises by 1.
- **Face-down:** allowed only when your score is at least 1; your power rises by `tokens[i]` and your score drops by 1.

You may stop at any time and leave tokens unused. Return the highest score you can reach at any point.
notes:
## Intuition

Every face-up play costs power and earns one point, and every face-down play gives power and costs one point. To make a point as cheap as possible, buy it with the **smallest** token left; to make a lost point worth as much as possible, trade it for the **largest** token left. After sorting, the cheapest tokens sit on the left and the richest on the right, so two pointers walking inward carry out this greedy. Trying every order of plays (the brute force) would explore exponentially many states.

## Approach

1. Sort `tokens` ascending; set `left` to the first token, `right` to the last, and `score` and `best` to 0.
2. While tokens remain (`left <= right`):
   - If `power` covers `tokens[left]`, play it face-up, then record `score` in `best` if it is higher.
   - Otherwise, if `score > 0`, play `tokens[right]` face-down to gain power.
   - Otherwise nothing is playable, so stop.
3. Return `best`, because a final face-down trade can leave `score` lower than the best value it reached.

## Example 1, step by step

`tokens = [100]`, `power = 50`. With `left = 0` and `right = 0`, power 50 is less than 100, so no face-up play; `score` is 0, so no face-down play either. The loop breaks and `best = 0` is returned.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for the sort; the two pointers then make at most n moves.
- Space: O(1) beyond the sort.

## Pitfalls

- Return the best score seen, not the score at the end: the last move may be a useless face-down trade.
- Break when neither move is possible, or the loop never ends.
- When `left === right`, there is a single token left; trading it face-down can never raise the score, which is why tracking `best` keeps the answer right.
- Tokens worth 0 are free points; with `power = 0` they can still be played face-up.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `left` | smallest token not yet used, the next one to buy a point with |
| `right` | largest token not yet used, the next one to trade for power |
| `power` | current energy |
| `score` | current score |
| `best` | highest score reached so far |

narration.2: Sort so the cheapest tokens are on the left and the most valuable on the right.
narration.3: left points at the smallest unused token, the cheapest way to buy a point.
narration.4: right points at the largest unused token, the best trade for power.
narration.6: best remembers the highest score reached, since later trades can lower the score.
narration.8: Keep playing while at least one token is unused.
narration.9: Can we afford the smallest token face-up?
narration.10: Yes: pay its value in power...
narration.13: Record the score if it is the best so far.
narration.14: Too little power, but we have a point to spend.
narration.15: Play the largest token face-down to gain the most power for that point.
narration.19: No move is possible, so stop.
narration.22: Return the highest score reached at any moment.
